Marta / Naomi —

Thanks for the details and the annotated dataflow. A few legal points after an initial pass (keeping short so we can iterate on the call):
1) KMS/EU key residency: Redwood can accept EU-only keys for production customer content. We need Novus to confirm this in a short focused exhibit (1 paragraph) that will be appended to the SCCs. That exhibit should state which data classes are covered (e.g., \"customer content\", \"user identifiers\") and explicitly exclude pseudonymised telemetry.
2) Incident SLA: 72 hours initial notification is acceptable as a floor, but Redwood is going to ask for an SLA tier for critical PII incidents of 24 hours for initial notification. We’ll propose a two-tier notification: 24h for critical PII, 72h for other incidents.
3) Subprocessor transparency: the redline we returned asks for 30-day notice of new subprocessors. Novus’s note references tiers — can Novus confirm whether tiered notice windows are an option (e.g., immediate for critical subprocessors, 30 days for others)?

I uploaded a tracked-change version with in-line comments to the Drive link Naomi circulated (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cNovus-DPA-evidence). I’ll also drop the tracked Word here after legal sync.
